newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MINERS STRIKE IN NSW
The union representing mine workers is blaming the Minerals Council for the strike that's hit mines throughout New South Wales.
Mine workers went out indefinately last night over an Opposition amendment in the State's Upper House which included them in a 25 percent cut to workers compensation payouts.
Union organiser Mick Watson says a section of the Minerals Council lobbied the opposition, after the Government had planned to exempt miners from the compensation limit.
It's estimated the stoppage will cost New South Wales A$12.5 million a day.
BREWERY TOLD TO DEVELOP RECYCLING SCHEME
Carlton and United Breweries have been given six months to develop a scheme to recycle used beer bottles and cans.
The order comes from the Environment Protection Authority as part of an EPA campaign to develop so-called "cradle to grave" industry responsibilty for its products.
The EPA recently placed a similar demand on the glass manufacturer ACI.
The move on CUB follows its decision to package some products in plastic bottles, something which the EPA says came without consultation with the environmental watchdog.
EMPLOYERS BACK EIGHT DOLLAR RISE FOR LOW PAID
Two big employer groups have come out in support of the Federal Government's submission for an eight-dollar-a-week rise for low paid workers.
The Metal Trades Industry Association and the Chamber of Manufactures back the Government's submission in response to the ACTU's living wage claim.
Employer groups say rise sought by the ACTU would seriously threaten the health of the economy.
MTIA Chief Executive Bob Herbert says the eight dollar rise would be targetted at employees who hasn't won an increase in enterprise bargaining.
He says it would also ensure an outcome in line with inflation which is trending down.
The Industrial Commission hears the case next month.
BID TO SAVE BABY DOLPHIN CONTINUES
Rescuers expect it'll be a few days before a dolphin stranded on a beach on the New South Wales south coast can be reunited with its family.
They've spend the night on the beach north of Jervis Bay monitoring the condition of the baby, which was caught in fishing nets two days ago.
National Parks and Wildlife rangers say the dolphin is still too tired from its ordeal to be released.
EVIDENCE FINISHING IN BLACKHAWK INQUIRY
The Inquiry into the collision of two army Black Hawk helicopters near Townsville in June, finishes hearing evidence today.
Final submissions from officers who could be adversely affected will be presented next week.
The inquiry was told yesterday that just days before the tragedy, the Director of Aviation was concerned there would be a mid air collision at night.
Colonel Robert Walford said there had been three incidents including one involving the Prime Minister, prior to the June crash in which 18 soldiers died.
The inquiry heard he'd told a fellow officer he was concerned there'd be a mid air collision on night vision goggles .. just days later those fears realised.
RUXTON ON IMMIGRATION...
The RSL has urged the Federal Government to re-think its immigration policies.
A motion to this effect has been moved by the Victorian branch, and passed unanimously, at a meeting of the League's national executive.
Victorian president Bruce Ruxton says the Government should listen to the overwhelming views of the Australian people, rather than vocal ethnic minorities and other lobby groups.
GOOD NEWS FOR BUILDING SOCIETIES
Australia's building societies have experienced a spurt in the growth of deposits.
The industry watchdog, the Australian Financial Institutions Commisison, says deposits totalling A$8.7 billion in the September quarter represented a 4.8 percent growth rate.
That followed several quarters of slow growth in deposits.
